script: I rode my bike, then the refuse lorry driver swerved—my life went to pieces.. I was riding my bike on a single‑lane road that got narrower over a bridge. I'd already been squeezing in front of the curb, trying not to crash into the pavement. Then a massive refuse lorry comes barreling through, like a bulldozer on wheels. He swerves right in front of me because he thought the oncoming car was going slower. My front wheel almost hit his rear wheel—two inches off—so I was literally fuming. (I know, right?) The lorry pulls left into a residential street, and I follow. I pull up right in front of him, all eyes on me as the crew starts unloading bins. I am not impressed with his lack of remorse, so I decide to "fix" it. I reach through the open window, snatch the keys, and toss them into a bush across the road. Then I keep riding. I told my partner, and she goes, "You're going to end up on Crimewatch, you're going to get reported, you're going to get in trouble." She's right—he's a big, tattoo‑covered guy who doesn't care about safety, and I am a 5ft4, skinny woman with a temper. (Literally insane.) In the end, I felt guilty. I regret pulling the keys out. The heat of the moment got the best of me. No one got hurt, but I know I crossed a line.
